title: SecOps compact audit pack and exception acknowledgement
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-ready audit pack to be attached to any production deployment that changes RBAC v2 mappings, audit log schema, SIEM export pipelines, or introduces exception approvals. It doubles as a launch checklist and a minimal evidence bundle for SOC/Compliance review. The intent is to be short (one page) for release engineers and SecOps reviewers, with links to full artifacts.

Quick summary checklist (must be completed before tag: production-deploy):
1) RBAC v2 changes:
   - Verified role definitions are least-privilege and scoped to specific resources (roles reviewed by 2 engineers + one product owner) — evidence: role-diff JSON and review comments.
   - Time-limited grants: any temporary elevation uses time-bound grant token or ephemeral role; expiry set and tested.
   - Service accounts: keys rotated or not introduced; if new SA created, key policy and rotation schedule attached.
   - Delegation matrix updated in IAM repo and PR link included.
   - RBAC change logged to audit stream with actor, role_before, role_after, reason_id.

2) Audit log schema validation:
   - Schema version bumped (audit_schema.v) and committed.
   - Required fields present: event_id, ts_utc, actor_id, actor_type, resource_id, resource_type, action, action_context, outcome, request_hash, response_code, request_latency_ms, trace_id.
   - PII flags included where applicable (pii_masking = true/false).
   - Test vector produced: sample_event.json validated against schema and ingested to staging SIEM.

3) SIEM export and pipeline checks:
   - Export format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with UTF-8; compressed using gzip for bulk export.
   - Transport checked: TLS 1.2+ or mTLS to ingestion endpoint; certificate fingerprints recorded.
   - Index mapping validated: field types match schema (ts -> date, actor_id -> keyword, action -> keyword).
   - Latency SLO: export lag < 60s for non-bulk events (test measured).
   - Alert correlation test: create synthetic event to trigger a pre-configured rule and verify dashboard alerting.

4) Evidence automation and bundling:
   - Evidence bundle generated automatically on PR merge: includes role-diff, schema diff, sample events, export logs (last 24h), deployment manifest, and CI artifact hashes.
   - Bundle signed with pipeline key (GPG/OIDC attestation): signature file present.
   - Evidence stored in secure bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/collections/<deploy-id> with server-side encryption and retention policy.
   - Automation badge posted to #secops-release Slack with link to bundle.

5) Exception approval pattern (when a hard requirement cannot be met):
   - Create JIRA ticket with prefix SEC-EXC and tag the deployment ticket.
   - Include: justification, compensating controls, estimated expiry, risk owner, and mitigation plan.
   - Required approvers: Risk Manager (secops), Product Security, SRE owner. Documented approvers must sign in the ticket and the evidence bundle.
   - Exceptions automatically expire after the stated expiry date; re-review required to extend.

Acceptance criteria (all must be YES or linked to an open SEC-EXC ticket):
- RBAC changes reviewed and merged: YES/NO -> evidence link
- Audit schema updated and regression tested: YES/NO -> evidence link
- SIEM export passing ingest and mapping checks: YES/NO -> evidence link
- Evidence bundle generated and signed: YES/NO -> evidence link
- No critical alerts triggered by test events: YES/NO -> notes

Quick runbook for reviewers:
- Open the evidence bundle link in the Slack message or S3.
- Spot-check 3 sample events: confirm actor_id and action mapping align with the change.
- Confirm schema version in bundle matches the deployed service config.
- Check SIEM index mapping in staging/production and run the synthetic alert test.
- If exception ticket exists, confirm compensating controls are in place and attach a mitigation verification screenshot.

Sign-off template (copy into release ticket):
- Release ID: <release-id>
- RBAC reviewer: <name> — signature/confirmation timestamp
- Audit schema reviewer: <name> — signature/confirmation timestamp
- SIEM owner: <name> — signature/confirmation timestamp
- SecOps approver (final): <name> — signature/confirmation timestamp

Exception example (for audit):
- SEC-EXC-2026-112: Temporarily allow encrypted debug-logs to include hashed user_ids for latency tracing. Compensating controls: logs restricted via tag, retention 7 days, SIEM alert on access, review weekly. Approval: Risk Manager, Product Security. Expiry: 2026-03-01. Evidence: attached bundle.

Post-deploy verification (24–72 hours):
- Confirm RBAC changes did not create unexpected 403s (monitor error spike dashboard).
- Confirm audit stream event rate consistent with baseline (no drops).
- Check SIEM ingestion error logs and export latency metrics.
- Trigger a re-bundle to capture initial production window and upload to evidence store.

Notes and links:
- Full RBAC v2 design: CONFLUENCE-SECOPS-4572
- Audit schema repo: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-schema (PR link in linked_artifacts)
- SIEM runbook and index definitions: CONFLUENCE-SIEM-1102
- Automation action: infra/actions/gen-evidence-bundle (GitHub Action)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical request_hash algorithm (sha256 vs blake2b) for audit logs — recommendation: sha256 for cross-tool compatibility.
- Add automated PI/PHI redaction test in the bundle generator.

Prepared by: Maya Chen (SecOps) — contact maya@redwood.com
Reviewer notes: please update this doc if any of the quick checks become flaky or if automation moves to a different repo.
